filings.title: April 2026 rebase, part 3
filings.summary: Rounding or measuring a span in months from the 29th, 30th or 31st can answer against the wrong pair of dates, because the polyfill never rechecks that the window it searched contains the date it is aiming for. The maintainer had already written this fix, so rather than file a duplicate we added what it was missing: a way to reproduce the bug, a scan of Chromium 153 against the published release, and before-and-after measurements of the fix applied on main.

filings.title: Polyfill: Validate result in UTC fast path in GetPossibleEpochNanoseconds
filings.summary: Near the end of the supported range, a calculation in the UTC time zone quietly returns a wrong value where it should report an error. The shortcut the code takes for UTC skips the range check that every other time zone goes through.
filings.outcome: Closed, not rejected: the maintainer is applying the upstream changes in order and asked to keep it that way, so this one arrives in its turn rather than ahead of it.

filings.title: Polyfill: Update Meiji era start date
filings.summary: The Japanese calendar puts dates from 1868 to the end of 1872 in the Meiji era, where the standard asks for the Gregorian-equivalent era. The era and era-year are wrong for those five years.
filings.outcome: Closed, not rejected: the maintainer is applying the upstream changes in order and asked to keep it that way, so this one arrives in its turn rather than ahead of it.

filings.title: Polyfill: Fix extreme PlainYearMonth crash in non-ISO calendars
filings.summary: Converting a Hebrew, Islamic, Coptic-family or Indian calendar date near either end of the supported range fails with an Invalid ISO date error, even though the date asked for is a real one.
filings.outcome: Closed, not rejected: the maintainer is applying the upstream changes in order and asked to keep it that way, so this one arrives in its turn rather than ahead of it.

filings.title: Don't format dates past the range limit when counting months in until()
filings.summary: Counting months between two dates in a non-ISO calendar fails when the later date falls in the first or last month of the supported range. The month-by-month loop builds a date beyond the range that it never actually needs.
filings.outcome: Closed, not rejected: the maintainer will apply the fix to the Temporal standard first, and it reaches the polyfill from there.

filings.title: Search the last partial window when looking for the next time zone transition
filings.summary: Looking for the next time zone transition in roughly the last two months of the supported range can report that there is none, when there is one. startOfDay, hoursInDay and toZonedDateTime then fail instead of returning an answer.
filings.outcome: Closed, not rejected: the maintainer will apply the fix to the Temporal standard first, and it reaches the polyfill from there.

filings.title: Start the time zone transition search before the first transition in 1844
filings.summary: Time zone lookups before 1847 miss a real transition on 31 December 1844 in five zones: Asia/Manila and four Pacific zones. The search starts at 1847, which used to be the earliest transition anyone had recorded and no longer is.
filings.outcome: Closed, not rejected: the maintainer will apply the fix to the Temporal standard first, and it reaches the polyfill from there.

filings.title: Release request: main has fixes that 0.5.1 doesn't (ZonedDateTime near the Instant limits, #341, #347)
filings.summary: Anyone using the published 0.5.1 release still meets several bugs that were fixed 76 commits ago on the project's main branch, among them failures for valid zoned dates near both ends of the range and two calendar-conversion bugs. No release has been published to bring those fixes to them.

filings.title: Polyfill: non-ISO until() by months gives wrong results since #3245, and throws near the range limits
filings.summary: Counting months between two dates in a non-ISO calendar has given a wrong answer since a recent change, at ordinary dates as well as unusual ones. Adding the answer back to the first date no longer lands on the second, and near the ends of the range the count fails outright.

filings.title: Polyfill: GetNamedTimeZoneNextTransition misses a transition in the last search window before the max Instant
filings.summary: Looking for the next time zone transition in the last stretch before the end of the supported range can report that there is none, when there is one. Code that relies on the answer then fails instead of getting one.

filings.title: Polyfill: calendarToIsoDate overshoot assertion from #3292 is reachable in coptic/ethiopic/ethioaa month 13
filings.summary: Building a Coptic, Ethiopic or Ethioaa date in the thirteenth month can fail an internal check instead of returning the date. The search moves eight days at a time, on the assumption that it can never step over a whole month, but that month is only five or six days long.
filings.gmtNote: GMT computes coptic and ethiopic dates through ethioaa and finds a date from its calendar fields by bisection, so this search-step bug can't affect it. A canary check (D10) watches for it in every polyfill release.

filings.title: Polyfill: time zone transitions before 1847 are not found (Asia/Manila and four Pacific zones on 1844-12-31)
filings.summary: Time zone lookups before 1847 miss a real transition on 31 December 1844 in five zones: Asia/Manila and four Pacific zones. The search assumes no zone has a transition before 1847, which the time zone database contradicts.

filings.title: ZonedDateTime.from rejects ZonedDateTime.prototype.toString's output when the local date is -271821-04-19
filings.summary: A zoned date and time in the first hours of the supported range, in a time zone west of Greenwich, prints as a string that reading it back then refuses. The spec checks the local date against the date range before it matches the offset, so the string fails although the moment it names is in range. The issue asks whether that check is meant.
filings.gmtNote: GMT follows the spec text here, as Chromium, Node and the polyfill do, so there is no workaround to retire. Its zoned readers (isValidZonedDateTime, toOffsetInstant, classifyStoredZoned and the rest) refuse a string whose local date is -271821-04-19. If the spec drops the check, they drop it too.
filings.outcome: Closed as answered: the check is intended. The Temporal champions had already said so on #3014, and it can go once tc39/ecma262#3464 lands.

filings.title: Polyfill: getTimeZoneTransition throws a bisection assertion for Africa/El_Aaiun in 1976
filings.summary: Looking for the next or previous time zone transition in Africa/El_Aaiun in spring 1976 can throw an internal assertion instead of answering. Two transitions there are just under 17 days apart, and the search window for that zone is 17 days, so one window can hold both. The issue proposes a 16-day window.

filings.title: Polyfill: Temporal.Now reads a millisecond before Date.now() after a pre-1970 clock reading
filings.summary: After the clock reads a date before 1970, the next Temporal.Now reading can land a millisecond before Date.now(), so a 2027 clock can read as the last millisecond of 2026. The polyfill carries the previous reading's milliseconds modulo a million as a sub-millisecond part, and the remainder keeps its minus sign. Fake timers in tests hit this whenever they set a pre-1970 date. The issue proposes a floor modulo.

filings.title: Failed Assert in NudgeToCalendarUnit when a duration ends in the later pass of a repeated hour
filings.summary: Measuring a length in days or weeks across a repeated or skipped hour can fail an internal check in the spec, when the length ends just past the edge of a day or week. The spec places that edge with the "compatible" rule, which can put it on the wrong side of the end, and its second try cannot move a day or week edge. Chromium throws and the polyfill returns a number the spec does not give, so GMT returns its sentinel for these lengths. The issue asks which answer is meant.

filings.title: `PlainDate.from` accepts malformed RFC 9557 annotations
filings.summary: Date parsing accepts strings RFC 9557 rejects: an empty annotation such as `2024-10-03[]`, a calendar annotation before the time zone, or an annotation value containing `;` or `=`.
filings.gmtNote: GMT runs on `@js-temporal/polyfill`, which gets this right, so this can't affect GMT. GMT's weekly swap check runs its tests on every new `temporal-polyfill` release.
filings.outcome: Closed as fixed: released in temporal-polyfill 1.0.7.

filings.title: `ZonedDateTime.from` rejects the two instants at the ends of the `Instant` range
filings.summary: `ZonedDateTime.from` rejects the two exact instants at the ends of Temporal's range, such as `-271821-04-20T00:00:00Z[Asia/Tokyo]`, which the standard accepts.
filings.gmtNote: GMT runs on `@js-temporal/polyfill`, which gets this right, so this can't affect GMT. GMT's weekly swap check runs its tests on every new `temporal-polyfill` release.
filings.outcome: Closed as fixed: released in temporal-polyfill 1.0.7.

filings.title: Wrong UTC offset all through the period between two close offset changes (follow-up to #73)
filings.summary: When a zone's offset changes twice within a few weeks, the polyfill skips the period between the changes and reads the wrong offset all through it, as in `Africa/Casablanca` during Ramadan in 2018. A daily check of every zone found it in 11 zones.
filings.gmtNote: GMT runs on `@js-temporal/polyfill`, which gets this right, so this can't affect GMT. GMT's weekly swap check runs its tests on every new `temporal-polyfill` release.
filings.outcome: Closed as fixed: released in temporal-polyfill 1.0.7.

filings.title: `getTimeZoneTransition("previous")` skips every transition more than three years after today
filings.summary: Searching back for a zone's last transition never returns one later than about three years from today. From any later date it returns an older transition, so the answer depends on the day the code runs.
filings.gmtNote: GMT runs on `@js-temporal/polyfill`, which gets this right, so this can't affect GMT. GMT's weekly swap check runs its tests on every new `temporal-polyfill` release.
filings.outcome: Closed as fixed: released in temporal-polyfill 1.0.8.

filings.title: Time zone transitions before 1847 are not found (`Asia/Manila` and four Pacific zones on 1844-12-31)
filings.summary: Transitions before 1847 are not found, so `Asia/Manila` and four Pacific zones miss their offset change on 31 December 1844.
filings.outcome: Closed as fixed: released in temporal-polyfill 1.0.8.

filings.title: Persian calendar: 78 years from 1502 to 2987 AP get the wrong leap year
filings.summary: The Persian calendar uses the plain 33-year leap rule, where ICU4X corrects 78 years from 1502 to 2987 AP. In the year after each one, every date reads one day early.
filings.gmtNote: GMT runs on `@js-temporal/polyfill`, which gets these Persian years right, so this can't affect GMT. GMT's weekly swap check compares each calendar's years with native Temporal on every new `temporal-polyfill` release.

filings.title: Chinese and Dangi: dates read from Intl differ from native Temporal (Chinese New Year 2027)
filings.summary: Chinese and Dangi dates are read from `Intl`, which on Node 26 (ICU 78.3) disagrees with native Temporal. Chinese New Year 2027 falls on 7 February instead of 6 February.
filings.gmtNote: GMT runs on `@js-temporal/polyfill`, which throws on Chinese and Dangi dates under ICU 78 instead (js-temporal/temporal-polyfill#360). GMT's weekly swap check compares each calendar's years with native Temporal on every new `temporal-polyfill` release.

filings.title: Apply the ICU4X leap-year corrections to the Persian calendar
filings.summary: Adds the 78 leap-year corrections that ICU4X, and so native Temporal, makes to the Persian calendar from 1502 to 2987 AP. Without them, every date in the year after each corrected year reads one day early, and the leap-year answers are wrong for both years.
filings.gmtNote: GMT runs on `@js-temporal/polyfill`, which gets these Persian years right, so this can't affect GMT. GMT's weekly swap check compares each calendar's years with native Temporal on every new `temporal-polyfill` release.

filings.title: Compute the Chinese and Dangi calendars like ICU4X instead of reading Intl
filings.summary: Computes Chinese and Dangi dates the way ICU4X, and so native Temporal, does, from its year tables for 1900 to 2102 and its mean-motion rule outside them, instead of reading them from the host's `Intl`. Dates no longer change with the host's ICU version, and dates near the end of Temporal's range no longer throw. It also fixes `until` and `since` from a leap month the end year lacks.
filings.gmtNote: GMT runs on `@js-temporal/polyfill`, which throws on Chinese and Dangi dates under ICU 78 instead (js-temporal/temporal-polyfill#360). GMT's weekly swap check compares each calendar's years with native Temporal on every new `temporal-polyfill` release.
